The core duality in partner policy lies in the separation of approval mechanisms—partner and offer approval operate independently. This creates a Cartesian product space (P, O) where each axis represents a distinct binary state. The validity of an offer is conditional on partner status, forming a logical constraint: V = O ∧ ¬(E ∨ R ∨ S ∨ ¬P). This implies that even if an offer is approved, it becomes invalid if the partner is expired, rejected, suspended, or not approved. The sponsor control boundary introduces a topological constraint in the decision space, ensuring that certain variables (e.g., model outputs, betting decisions) remain invariant under sponsor influence. These primitives form a structured lattice in GSE’s state space and define Bayesian conditioning sets in GSI’s probabilistic framework.
